headline: Clinton order sets up how the U.S. carries out its role in two U.S.-Mexico border environment and development institutions.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order deals with putting into effect U.S. participation in the Border Environment Cooperation Commission and the North American Development Bank. These two groups were created under a 1993 agreement between the United States and Mexico to help plan and pay for environmental projects, such as water and wastewater systems, near the border. No summary was provided, so the order's exact details, such as which federal agencies were given which duties, are not described here.

who_it_affects.how: They are the main areas these two institutions were set up to serve with environmental infrastructure projects.
The order likely assigns agencies responsibilities for managing U.S. involvement in the two institutions, though the specifics are not given.
